unmapped_findings: Experimental flow-stress behavior of this sample (950 °C, 0.1→0.01 s^-1 at ε=0.2): after the transient strain-rate drop, the experimental stress falls within about a 0.04 strain interval to a level lower than that of the 0.01 s^-1 constant-deformation condition; Model 1 delays the predicted softening while Model 2 reproduces it (Fig. 8c/8d, b0187).

Table 7 (3D CA simulation): for 950 °C, 0.1–0.01 s^-1 (0.2 strain) at 0.9 strain, final AGS = 52.10 μm vs the constant 950 °C, 0.01 s^-1 baseline of 52.52 μm — indicating a transient decrease of Z_p has little effect on the final grain size (b0251, table_007).

Table 7 (3D CA simulation): this sample has DRXGs_I AGS = 34.82 μm (volume fraction 0.02) and DRXGs_II AGS = 52.57 μm (volume fraction 0.97); the residual DRXGs_I fraction is low after transiently decreasing Z_p (b0251, b0252).

Discussion (Fig. 24a/24c): for the transient strain-rate decrease 0.1→0.01 s^-1 at 950 °C (ε_I=0.2), first-stage DRXGs_I grow rapidly after the drop and are later refined by second-stage DRXGs_II; matrix grains retain higher dislocation density than in the constant 0.01 s^-1 case, promoting further DRX growth (b0240, figure_024).

Aggregate accuracy of the 3D CA model under varying deformation conditions (Table 5, all varying-condition tests): flow stress RMSE 3.3118 MPa, R² 0.9589, AARE 4.57 %; AGS RMSE 4.0169 μm, R² 0.9777, AARE 4.11 %; DRX fraction RMSE 0.0229, R² 0.9784, AARE 2.47 % (b0222, b0223, figure_unlabelled_005).
